convoLines.text: "Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that. Let's move."
"Luke is gone and Nathan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I keep turning over the last thing Nathan said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Meera grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Meera is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire feels smaller without Nathan. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
«Добре сказано. Саме так.» (you catch 'сказано' — said) They nod back, a little quicker this time. "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Все буде добре.» (you catch 'добре' — good) They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
«Я цього тобі ніколи не забуду.» (you catch 'забуду' — forget) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «У тебе є їжа? Щось?» (Do you have food? Something? — you're fairly sure)
Onufriy blinks. Then cracks up. "You said that BEAUTIFULLY. It means nothing like what you think it means." They teach you the right word, still laughing.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about grief — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that. Let's move.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Meera has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about The Focus Group last night — what to even CALL it. 'Loud-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Добре, що ти тут. Справді.» (Good that you're here. Really. — you're fairly sure)
It's quiet at the tree line. Onufriy doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
«Погоджуюся з тобою.» (I agree with you. — you're fairly sure) They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«Дякую, що ти тут.» (Thanks that you're here. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Ти справді добра людина.» (You're truly a good person. — you're fairly sure) You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «Ти розумієш?» (Do you understand? — you're fairly sure)
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.

"Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you."
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"

"Alright. Catch you later."

lines: d39: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Luke Schumacher is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d39: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d39: 🕯️ Luke Schumacher is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d39: What Luke kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d39: "Luke's gone." Nathan looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Luke." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d39: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Frieda blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d39: 📖 LEARNED: Stalk (Level 1). Move unseen. Close distance without being noticed.
d39: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d39: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Luke Schumacher, 39 days. The mantle passes to Frieda Singh.
d39: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Frieda Singh, 36 — an aquarium keeper. Their hands know different work now: Bloodhound, Lucky Rock, Bird Whisperer, Trophy Room.
d39: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Stalker of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d39: The village's quarrel was with Luke — and Luke is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d39: At the grave, Meera, Nathan, Onufriy and 3 more speak for Frieda — "Luke trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d39: The fire knew Frieda before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
